title: Rural Home Loans Late Charge Floor: Questions on Loan Seasoning
content:
Rural Home Loans: the smallest late charge depends on the member's standing on the home loan.

## The rule

A loan open more than 60 months with no late charge that counts toward the rate has a floor of 10.00 USD; a loan open more than 60 months with one or more late charges that count has a floor of 12.50 USD; any other loan has the product's minimum late charge as its floor. A late charge figured below the floor is raised to the floor.

## Questions and answers

**How are the months open counted?** In whole months from the loan's opening date on the loan record to today, a month being completed on the same day of the month as the opening date.

**Which late charges count?** The late charges assessed on the home loan in the twelve months up to today less the late-charge waivers recorded on the home loan in those twelve months, whether granted as an error correction or as a courtesy. The twelve months run from the day after the same calendar day twelve months before today through today.

**Is a loan open exactly 60 months seasoned?** No. The test is more than 60 months; at exactly 60 months the floor is the product's minimum late charge, and at 61 months the seasoned floors apply.

**What does the floor change?** Only the smallest amount a late charge may be; a figure at or above the floor is not changed by it.

## Floor table

| Months open | Late charges that count | Floor |
|---|---|---|
| 61 or more | none | 10.00 |
| 61 or more | one or more | 12.50 |
| 60 or fewer | any | the product's minimum late charge |

## Worked case (hypothetical inputs)

A loan opened 72 whole months ago with one late charge assessed and one waived in the twelve months has no late charge that counts, so its floor is 10.00; a figured charge of 8.40 is raised to 10.00, and a figured charge of 11.25 stays 11.25.
